stem: A 3-month-old girl is brought for a well-child visit. When placed prone she lifts her head off the table. She does not smile when her mother's face comes close and has not made any cooing or gurgling sounds. The rest of the examination is normal.
oneliner: 3-month-old F + lifts head when prone + no social smile + no cooing → which domains are delayed?
ask: Which of the following best describes her development for age?

options.A: Normal motor, normal social, normal verbal
options.B: Delayed motor, delayed social, delayed verbal
options.C: Normal motor, delayed social, normal verbal
options.D: Delayed motor, normal social, delayed verbal
options.E: Normal motor, delayed social, delayed verbal

whyNot.A: She **does not smile or coo**, so social and verbal cannot both be called normal
whyNot.B: She **lifts her head when prone**, so motor is not delayed
whyNot.C: The **absent cooing** means verbal is delayed too, not only social
whyNot.D: She **lifts her head** (motor normal) but **does not smile** (social delayed), the reverse of this pattern

answer: Normal motor, delayed social and verbal development
why: By **3 months** an infant lifts the head when prone, gives a **social smile** and **coos**. She meets the motor goal but misses the **social** and **verbal** ones.

idea.rule: Check each domain separately: motor, social and verbal milestones can be out of step with each other.
also: 4 months: rolls over, orients to voice
10 months: stands, says mama and dada

stem: A 20-month-old girl walks and runs well and uses many words. Her mother is worried because at playdates she plays alone beside the other children, and yesterday she hit a boy who tried to share her toy. She makes eye contact and points to show her mother objects.
oneliner: 20-month-old F + walks, runs, many words + plays alone beside others + hit a child over a toy + eye contact → which?
ask: Which of the following best explains her behavior?

options.A: Early signs of autism spectrum disorder
options.B: Normal parallel play for her age

whyNot.A: She has **good language, eye contact and pointing to show objects**, which argue against autism
whyNot.C: ODD needs **6 months of defiance toward adults**; one fight over a toy with another child is not that
whyNot.D: Conduct disorder means **repeated violation of others' rights or rules**, not a single toddler conflict
whyNot.E: ADHD needs **inattention or hyperactivity across settings**, which are not described

why: At about **18 months to 2 years** children play **alongside**, not with, each other and may grab or hit over toys. **Cooperative play** is not expected until about **3 to 4 years**.

idea.rule: Toddler play is solitary or parallel; sharing and cooperative play come years later.

stem: A 9-month-old boy born at 32 weeks' gestation is seen for a well-child visit. His mother is worried because he has only just started to sit without support. He is interactive and his examination is normal.
oneliner: 9-month-old M + born at 32 weeks + just sits without support + interactive, normal exam → which age to judge him by?
ask: Which age should be used to judge his milestones?

options.A: Chronologic age of 9 months, so he is delayed by about 3 months
options.B: Gestational age at birth plus 9 months, so he is on track
options.C: Corrected age of 7 months, so his development is normal
options.D: Corrected age only until 3 months, then chronologic age
options.E: Bone age on a hand radiograph, which sets milestone timing

whyNot.A: Chronologic age ignores the **8 weeks he was born early**; judged this way a normal preterm infant looks delayed
whyNot.B: Adding to the **gestational age at birth** is not how any milestone age is calculated
whyNot.D: Correction continues to about **age 2**, so at 9 months it still applies
whyNot.E: Bone age measures **skeletal maturity**, not developmental milestones

answer: Corrected age (about 7 months), so sitting is normal
why: **Corrected age** = chronologic age minus the **weeks born early** (here 8 weeks), used until about **age 2**. At 7 months corrected age, **sitting without support** (expected by about 6 months) is normal.

idea.rule: Judge preterm infants by corrected age, not chronologic age, until about 2 years.
also: Corrected age = chronologic age minus weeks premature
Use it for milestones and growth charts
Sits without support by about 6 months

stem: A 2-year-old boy with recurrent otitis media is brought for a routine visit. He runs well and kicks a ball, speaks in three- to four-word sentences, pretends to care for his baby sister and is almost toilet trained. His growth is at the 50th percentile.
oneliner: 2-year-old M + recurrent otitis media + runs, kicks a ball + 3-4 word sentences + pretend play + almost toilet trained → which domains?
ask: Which of the following best describes his development?

options.A: Normal cognitive, normal social, normal motor
options.B: Delayed cognitive, normal social, normal motor
options.C: Normal cognitive, delayed social, normal motor
options.D: Delayed cognitive, delayed social, normal motor
options.E: Normal cognitive, normal social, delayed motor

whyNot.B: Three- to four-word sentences are **at or ahead of age**, so cognition and language are not delayed
whyNot.C: **Pretend play and caring for his sister** show normal social skills
whyNot.D: His **sentences** and **pretend play** are both on time, so neither domain is delayed
whyNot.E: He **runs well and kicks a ball**, which are on-time motor skills at 2 years

why: A 2-year-old normally **runs, kicks a ball** and joins **two words into phrases** (three-word sentences are expected by **age 3**), plays pretend and is starting **toilet training**. His development is **normal despite the ear infections**.

idea.rule: Compare the child with the milestones before blaming a risk factor.
also: 3 years: three-word sentences, rides a tricycle
Recurrent otitis media delays speech only if hearing is lost
